chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn al-Rayyān, who said:

Al-Maʾmūn employed every stratagem against Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), but he was unable to achieve anything concerning him. Then when he desired to give his daughter to him in marriage, he sent to two hundred maidservants from among the most beautiful there could be, with each one of them a goblet containing a jewel, to receive Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام).

When he sat in the place of the nobles, he did not turn toward them. And there was a man called Mukhāriq, a possessor of voice, lute, and rhythmic striking, with a long beard. Al-Maʾmūn summoned him, and he said, "O Commander of the Faithful, if it concerns anything from the affairs of the world, I shall suffice you regarding his matter." So he sat before Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام).

Then Mukhāriq gave a great cry, and the people of the house gathered around him, and he began striking his lute and singing. When he had done that for some time, and Abū Jaʿfar was not turning toward him, neither to the right nor to the left, then he raised his head toward him and said, "Fear Allah, O one with the little beard." He said: then the plectrum fell from his hand, and the lute as well, and he never had use of his hands until he died.
He said: then Al-Maʾmūn asked him about his condition, and he said, "When Abū Jaʿfar shouted at me, I was struck by a terror from which I shall never recover."

key_terms.اتَّقِ اللَّهَ: fear Allah; a direct moral rebuke
key_terms.احْتَالَ: devised stratagems or employed cunning plans
key_terms.الْمِضْرَابُ: the plectrum used to strike the strings of the lute
key_terms.عُودٍ: a lute or stringed musical instrument
key_terms.فَزِعْتُ: I was terrified or struck with fear
key_terms.مُخَارِقٌ: the named singer and musician brought before the Imam
key_terms.وَصِيفَةٍ: a maidservant or young female attendant

ai.seo_question: How does this narration show Imam al-Jawād’s detachment from worldly temptation and spiritual authority?
ai.summary: This report narrates how al-Maʾmūn tried various worldly means to affect Imam Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام), including luxury, beauty, and music, but none had any effect on him. The Imam’s spiritual authority is shown when a single rebuke from him overwhelms the singer Mukhāriq and leaves him permanently incapacitated. The narration highlights the Imam’s detachment from worldly temptation and his awe-inspiring presence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Muhammad Bin Al Rayyan who said,

‘Al-Mamoun cajoled Upon Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> (9<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) with every ploy but he was not enabled upon anything with regards to it. So when he was frustrated and intended to marry his daughter to him<sup>asws</sup>, sent two hundred bridesmaids from the most beautiful as could happen to be, a bowl for each one of them wherein was a jewel, to welcome Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>.

When he<sup>asws</sup> was seated in a choicest place, he<sup>asws</sup> did not turn towards them, and there was a man called Mukhariq, owner of the (good) voice, and a lute, and beat, of a long beard. So Al-Mamoun called him over, and he said, ‘O commander of the faithful! If it was regarding anything from the affairs of the world, so I shall suffice you of his<sup>asws</sup> matter’. So he sat in front of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>.

Mukhariq inhaled with an inhalation (to sing) and the people of the house gathered, and he went on to strike on his lute and sing. So when he had done so for a while and when Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> did not turn towards him, neither right nor left, then he<sup>asws</sup> raised his<sup>asws</sup> head and said: ‘Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, O one with the goatee (beard)!’. So the drum fell from his hand and the lute. So he did not benefit by his hands until (up to the day) he died.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So Al-Mamoun asked about his sate. He said, ‘When Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> shouted at me, I panicked with such a panic, I shall not be coming out from it, ever!’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of our people from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan who has said the following

“Al-Ma’mun did all he could to prove that abu Ja‘far, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (a.s.) was only a young man of worldly desires. However Al-Ma’mun could not succeed. When he became frustrated he gave his daughter in marriage to abu Ja‘far, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (a.s.). For the ceremony he sent two hundred most beautiful entertaining girls each with a bowl in her hand with a precious pearl in it to well come abu Ja‘far, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (a.s.) when he would sit on the special seat prepared for him. They, however, were not of any attraction to the Imam (a.s.) to disturb him.

There was a man called Mukhariq who had a voice, musical skills, a guitar and a tall beard. Al-Ma’mun called him and he said, “O Amir al-Mu’minin, if he is a worldly man I will prove myself as dealing him deadly blows on your behalf.” He sat in front of abu Ja‘far, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (a.s.)

and began to bray a hee-haw that made all the people of the house gather around him. He began to play his guitar and sing. He did it for an hour but abu Ja‘far (a.s.) did not pay any attention to the right or left. Then he (a.s.) raised his head and said, “O you, tall bearded one, be pious before Allah.” The narrator has said that the musical instrument and guitar fell off his hand and he could not use his hands thereafter until he died.

When Al-Ma’mun asked him about his condition he said, “When abu Ja‘far (a.s.) expressed his disappointment at me it struck me with a huge degree of fear from which I have not been able to relieve myself ever since.”
